rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are plural because each is a distinct kind, while the earth is singular because all earths share the substance of soil.
rows.anchor: ذكر السماوات بلفظ الجمع والأرض بلفظ الواحد لأن كل سماء ليست من جنس واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens signify their height without pillars and their sun, moon, and stars; the earth signifies its breadth and its trees, rivers, mountains, seas, minerals, and plants.
rows.anchor: فالآية في السماوات سمكها وارتفاعها من غير عمد ولا علاقة وما ترى فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day differ by succeeding one another; the verse parallels the description of them as alternating turns.
rows.anchor: أي تعاقبهما في الذهاب والمجيء يخلف أحدهما صاحبه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ataa explains their alternation as differences in light and darkness and in their increasing and decreasing lengths.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: أراد اختلافهما في النور والظلمة والزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is mentioned before day because it came first; the author cites the image of day being stripped from night.
rows.anchor: وقدم الليل على النهار في الذكر لأنه أقدم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulk means ships in either singular or plural; it is feminine when plural and masculine when singular, as the cited verses illustrate.
rows.anchor: واحده وجمعه سواء فإذا أريد به الجمع يؤنث وفي الواحد يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships are a sign through God's subjection of them to travel on the water while carrying loads without sinking; people benefit by riding and trading.
rows.anchor: تسخيرها وجريانها على وجه الماء وهي موقرة لا ترسب تحت الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain's 'heaven' may mean clouds, where God creates water before it falls, or the familiar heaven, from which it descends through clouds to earth.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد بالسماء السحاب، يخلق الله الماء في السحاب ثم من السحاب ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water revives the earth after its dryness and barrenness, while God disperses every kind of creature across it.
rows.anchor: أي بالماء {الأرض بعد موتها} أي بعد يبوستها وجدوبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'wind' in the singular; most readers use the plural, Abu Ja'far uses plural elsewhere, and readings vary except in the agreed cases cited.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي الريح بغير ألف وقرأ الباقون بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind shifts among south, north, east, west, and intermediary directions, and can be gentle, violent, hot, or cold.
rows.anchor: وتصريفها أنها تتصرف إلى الجنوب والشمال والقبول والدبور والنكباء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls wind and water the greatest of God's forces.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أعظم جنود الله الريح والماء

rows.speaker: شريح القاضي
rows.claim: Shurayh says every wind brings either relief to someone ill or illness to someone well.
rows.anchor: قال شريح القاضي: ما هبت ريح إلا لشفاء سقيم أو لسقم صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says eight winds divide into four of mercy and four of punishment; another names the merciful winds as the bearers, spreaders, scatterers, and senders.
rows.anchor: وقيل الرياح ثمانية: أربعة للرحمة وأربعة للعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cloud is named for its rapid movement, as though it were being dragged; the signs teach rational people that these things have a creator.
rows.anchor: سمي سحابا لأنه ينسحب أي يسير في سرعة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says the origin of thunder, lightning, and clouds is unknown.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: ثلاثة لا يدرى من أين تجيء الرعد والبرق والسحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath is a euphemism for sexual intercourse; Ibn Abbas says the Qur'anic terms for intimate contact likewise refer to intercourse.
rows.anchor: فالرفث كناية عن الجماع، قال ابن عباس: إن الله تعالى حيي كريم يكني

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says rafath broadly covers everything men desire from women.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الرفث كلمة جامعة لكل ما يريده الرجال من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At first, after breaking the fast one could eat, drink, and have intercourse only until the night prayer or sleep; then these acts were forbidden until the next night.
rows.anchor: كان في ابتداء الأمر إذا أفطر الرجل حل له الطعام والشراب والجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Umar had intercourse after the night prayer, he regretted it and asked the Prophet for relief; the Prophet replied that Umar was not worthy of that conduct, and others confessed similar acts before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: فأتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: يا رسول الله إني أعتذر إلى الله وإليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spouses are garments for one another, meaning sources of comfort; the author supports this with the verse that God made a mate so one could find repose in her.
rows.anchor: أي سكن لكم {وأنتم لباس لهن} أي سكن لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations compare spouses to a shared garment during sleep, or say each veils the other from what is forbidden; Rabi ibn Anas instead calls them bedding and coverlet.
rows.anchor: وقيل: سمي كل واحد من الزوجين لباسا لتجردهما عند النوم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and others say a woman may be called one's garment, bedding, or waist-wrapper; a hadith says marriage protects two thirds of one's religion.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة وغيره: يقال للمرأة هي لباسك وفراشك وإزارك

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara says that when Ramadan fasting was first prescribed, men abstained from wives throughout the month, and some wronged themselves by breaking that restriction.
rows.anchor: قال البراء: لما نزل صوم رمضان كانوا لا يقربون النساء رمضان كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former restriction was a betrayal and injustice to oneself; God relented, erased the sin, and then permitted intercourse.
rows.anchor: أي تخونونها وتظلمونها بالمجامعة بعد العشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashiruhunna means have lawful intercourse; it is called direct contact because the partners' skin touches.
rows.anchor: جامعوهن حلالا سميت المجامعة مباشرة لتلاصق بشرة كل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most exegetes understand 'seek what God wrote for you' as seeking a child; Mujahid says seek offspring, even with another wife if one does not conceive.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما كتب الله لكم في اللوح المحفوظ يعني الولد، قاله أكثر المفسرين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the phrase as seeking the dispensation God ordained: eating, drinking, and intercourse during the fast's nights.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: وابتغوا الرخصة التي كتب الله لكم بإباحة الأكل والشرب والجماع

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh interprets what God wrote as Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل: وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم يعني ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation followed an exhausting day of work by an unnamed account's Abu Sirma ibn Qays, or Abu Qays ibn Sirma according to Ikrima, or Abu Qays Sirma ibn Anas according to al-Kalbi; he fell asleep before eating and became dangerously weak.
rows.anchor: نزلت في رجل من الأنصار اسمه أبو صرمة بن قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white and black threads mean daylight and nighttime darkness; they were likened to threads because each first appears as an extended line.
rows.anchor: يعني بياض النهار من سواد الليل، سميا خيطين لأن كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl says the phrase was first revealed without 'of dawn'; some tied white and black threads to their legs, so the clarification 'of dawn' specified natural light and dark.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال: أنزلت {وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: Adi put a black and white cord beneath his pillow and watched them unsuccessfully; the Prophet explained that the words mean night's blackness and day's whiteness.
rows.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم قال: لما نزلت {حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الأبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting begins at true dawn, when eating and drinking cease, and ends at sunset, when the fast is broken.
rows.anchor: فالصائم يحرم عليه الطعام والشراب بطلوع الفجر الصادق ويمتد إلى غروب الشمس

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar reports the Prophet's rule that the fast is broken once night comes from the east, day recedes in the west, and the sun sets.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tikaf is remaining in a mosque in worship; it is a recommended practice, valid in any mosque, and not outside one.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف في الشرع هو الإقامة في المسجد على عبادة الله، وهو سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban addresses intercourse during i'tikaf, which is prohibited and invalidates the retreat; intercourse was forbidden day and night for the companions who left the mosque for it.
rows.anchor: فالجماع حرام في حال الاعتكاف ويفسد به الاعتكاف

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet observed the final ten days of Ramadan in i'tikaf until his death, and his wives continued the practice after him.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يعتكف العشر الأواخر من رمضان حتى توفاه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars, and al-Shafii's stronger view, consider kissing or touching with desire disliked but not invalidating i'tikaf; Malik says it invalidates it.
rows.anchor: فمكروه ولا يفسد به الاعتكاف عند أكثر أهل العلم وهو أظهر قولي الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says emission invalidates the retreat, while touch without emission does not, by analogy with fasting.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن أنزل بطل اعتكافه وإن لم ينزل فلا كالصوم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet would bring his head near her while in i'tikaf so she could groom him, and he entered the house only for a human need; the author uses this for non-desirous touch.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا اعتكف أدنى إلي رأسه فأرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stated limits are the fasting and i'tikaf rulings just described; 'limits' means what God has forbidden people to violate.
rows.anchor: تلك الأحكام التي ذكرها في الصيام والاعتكاف

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses God's limits as His conditions; Shahr ibn Hawshab calls them His obligations.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: شروط الله، وقال شهر بن حوشب: فرائض الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabic root of hadd is prevention, as a gatekeeper is called a haddad because he prevents entry.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحد في اللغة المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach the limits means do not commit the prohibited acts; God clarifies His signs so people may avoid them and escape punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا تأتوها {كذلك} هكذا {يبين الله آياته للناس لعلهم يتقون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse continues the preceding account of Abraham's disputant; another reading treats it as a separate question asking whether one has seen both men.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية منسوقة على الآية الأولى، تقديره {ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم}

rows.speaker: قتادة، عكرمة، الضحاك
rows.claim: Qatada, Ikrima, and al-Dahhak identify the passerby as Uzayr ibn Sharhiya.
rows.anchor: فقال قتادة وعكرمة والضحاك: هو عزير بن شرخيا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb identifies him as Armiya ibn Hilqiya, from Aaron's tribe, and says he was al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: هو أرميا بن حلقيا، وكان من سبط هارون، وهو الخضر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the passerby was an unbeliever who doubted resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو كافر شك في البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported locations for the village include Jerusalem, the holy land, Dayr Sabir Abad, Muslim Badh, Dayr Hiraql, a village destroyed with its fleeing inhabitants, and an "grape village" two farsakhs from Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في تلك القرية فقال وهب وعكرمة وقتادة: هي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawiya can describe a fallen or an empty house; the village lay collapsed on its roofs, with roofs falling first and walls then falling onto them.
rows.anchor: ساقطة يقال: خوي البيت بكسر الواو يخوي خوى، مقصورا، إذا سقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arush means roofs, though it can also refer to any structure; the image describes the walls falling over the collapsed roofs.
rows.anchor: على عروشها} سقوفها، واحدها عرش وقيل: كل بناء عرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the village's restoration, a call ordered the dead man to live; he rose and his donkey brayed, and God preserved Armiya's life in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: ثم نودي: إن الله يأمرك أن تحيا، فقام بإذن الله ونهق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He thought he had been dead a day because he died at midmorning and awoke late in the day a century later, before sunset.
rows.anchor: أماته ضحى في أول النهار وأحياه بعد مائة عام في آخر النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preserved food was figs and the drink was juice; they appeared freshly picked and pressed despite the century.
rows.anchor: يعني التين {وشرابك} يعني العصير

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i explains lam yatasannah as though years had not passed over it.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: كأنه لم تأت عليه السنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Yaqub omit the h in connected recitation; others retain it. The omitted h may be an added pause marker after an original yatasanna.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ويعقوب لم يتسن بحذف الهاء في الوصل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr derives yatasannah from a two-nun form meaning to change, as in the description of altered mud; the author also reports a view that the h is original to the word for year.
rows.anchor: هو من التسنن بنونين: وهو التغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular verb for the unspoiled food and drink refers to the nearer noun, drink, and suffices because both share the meaning.
rows.anchor: رد التغيير إلى أقرب اللفظين وهو الشراب واكتفى بذكر أحد المذكورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the man looked at the donkey, its bones were white; God joined them, clothed them with flesh and skin, and revived it before his eyes.
rows.anchor: فركب الله تعالى العظام بعضها على بعض فكساه اللحم والجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw in 'and to make you a sign' may be superfluous; al-Farra says it signals a condition for a following act, with the sense 'to make you a sign of resurrection.'
rows.anchor: قيل الواو زائدة مقحمة. وقال الفراء أدخلت الواو فيه دلالة

rows.speaker: الضحاك وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and others say he returned to his village as a young man, while his descendants were elderly and his hair remained black.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك وغيره: إنه عاد إلى قريته شابا وأولاده وأولاد أولاده شيوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hijaz and Basra readers read nunsiruha with an r, meaning revive the bones; others read nunshizuha with a z, meaning raise and reassemble them.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة ننشرها بالراء معناه نحييها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Most exegetes take the bones as the donkey's; al-Suddi describes winds gathering the scattered bones, God assembling them, then covering them with flesh before an angel revives the animal.
rows.anchor: فقال الأكثرون: أراد به عظام حماره، وقال السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another group says God did not kill the donkey but killed the man, restoring his eyes and head while his body remained dead; the donkey remained intact, so the text's order is inverted.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم أراد به عظام هذا الرجل، وذلك أن الله تعالى لم يمت حماره

rows.speaker: قتادة عن كعب، والضحاك عن ابن عباس، والسدي عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They narrate that Uzayr returned to find an ancient blind, lame woman who had known him; at his prayer she regained sight and mobility, recognized him, and summoned his son and descendants, who identified his birthmark.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة عن كعب والضحاك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi say Nebuchadnezzar had burned the Torah; an angel gave Uzayr water that imprinted the Torah in his chest, and he recited it to Israel, who then called him God's son.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي والكلبي: لما رجع عزير إلى قومه وقد أحرق بختنصر التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Israel's calling Uzayr God's son is deferred to the account in Surat al-Tawbah.
rows.anchor: وستأتي القصة في سورة براءة إن شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read 'know' as a connected jussive command from God to Uzayr; others read it as Uzayr's declarative statement after seeing the resurrection.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي مجزوما موصولا على الأمر على معنى قال الله تعالى له اعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means the reward of the spenders' charity, like a seed sown by a farmer, and 'God's path' may mean jihad or every kind of good.
rows.anchor: فيه إضمار تقديره مثل صدقات الذين ينفقون أموالهم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the hundred grains as what each planted grain produces, not necessarily a single visible head already holding a hundred grains.
rows.anchor: فقال: كل سنبلة أنبتت مائة حبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hundredfold head is possible even if not commonly seen; a conceivable, non-impossible case can serve as a parable.
rows.anchor: قيل: ذلك متصور، غير مستحيل، وما لا يكون مستحيلا جاز ضرب المثل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may multiply the seven-hundredfold return further, from seven to seventy, seven hundred, or whatever measure He wills beyond human knowledge.
rows.anchor: يضاعف على هذا ويزيد لمن يشاء ما بين سبع إلى سبعين إلى سبعمائة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasi means wealthy and giving abundantly; alim means knowing the intention of the person who spends.
rows.anchor: {والله واسع} غني يعطي عن سعة {عليم} بنية من ينفق ماله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about Uthman and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: the latter gave four thousand dirhams and retained four thousand for his family, and Uthman equipped the Tabuk army with a thousand camels.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: نزلت هذه الآية في عثمان بن عفان وعبد الرحمن بن عوف

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سمرة
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura reports that Uthman brought a thousand dinars for the army of hardship; the Prophet turned them over and said Ibn Affan's deeds would not harm him after that day.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن سمرة: جاء عثمان رضي الله عنه بألف دينار في جيش العسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is reminding the recipient of one's gift and enumerating one's favors so as to spoil them; harm includes reproaching or saying the recipient keeps asking and causing annoyance.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يمن عليه بعطائه فيقول أعطيتك كذا، ويعد نعمه عليه فيكدرها

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan says harm includes telling a recipient, 'I gave you and gave you; you were not grateful.'
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان: {منا ولا أذى} أن يقول قد أعطيتك وأعطيت فما شكرت

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd relays his father's advice to stop greeting a recipient if one's greeting burdens him; God forbids reminding people of favors, a reproach among humans but a divine favor and reminder from God.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: كان أبي يقول: إذا أعطيت رجلا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who give without reminding or harming receive their reward from God and have neither fear nor grief.
rows.anchor: {لهم أجرهم} أي ثوابهم {عند ربهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kind reply to a petitioner, or a kindly promise, is 'recognized speech'; al-Kalbi says it can be a prayer for a fellow believer in their absence, and al-Dahhak links it to reconciliation.
rows.anchor: أي كلام حسن ورد على السائل جميل

rows.speaker: الكلبي والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and al-Dahhak say forgiveness means overlooking the wrongdoer; it can also mean forgiving a poor person's rude persistence when refused.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي والضحاك: بتجاوز عن ظالمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by hurtful reminders or reproach.
rows.anchor: {خير من صدقة} يدفعها إليه {يتبعها أذى} أي من وتعيير للسائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no one's charity and, being forbearing, does not hasten punishment of one who reminds and hurts recipients.
rows.anchor: {والله غني} أي مستغن عن صدقة العباد {حليم} لا يعجل بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says charity is nullified by reminding God of one's gift, as well as by hurting the recipient.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: بالمن على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The show-off's gift resembles soil washed from a smooth stone: apparent deeds vanish on the Day of Judgment because they were not for God.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان يوم القيامة بطل كله واضمحل لأنه لم يكن لله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This comparison includes the hypocrite, the show-off, and the believer who reminds and hurts; they seem to have deeds as the stone seems to hold soil.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لنفقة المنافق والمرائي والمؤمن الذي يمن بصدقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers cannot obtain reward for what they earned, and God does not guide disbelieving people.
rows.anchor: {لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا} أي على ثواب شيء مما كسبوا

rows.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
rows.claim: Mahmud ibn Labid reports that the Prophet feared lesser shirk for his community and identified it as showing off; at judgment, God will direct show-offs to seek reward from those they performed for.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال "إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم الشرك الأصغر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spenders seek God's pleasure; Qatada glosses 'confirming themselves' as expecting reward, while al-Shabi and al-Kalbi say they give with sincere belief in God's promise.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: احتسابا، وقال الشعبي والكلبي: تصديقا من أنفسهم

rows.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ata and Mujahid read the phrase as placing or allocating their wealth; al-Hasan says they proceed with charity only once sure it is for God, holding back if doubt remains.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء ومجاهد: يثبتون أي يضعون أموالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this interpretation, tathbit means deliberation, like the related verbal form in the command to devote oneself to God.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول يكون التثبيت بمعنى التثبت

rows.speaker: المبرد والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Farra say a garden with palms is called janna, while one with grapevines is called firdaus.
rows.anchor: قال (المبرد) (1) والفراء: إذا كان في البستان نخل فهو جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Amir and Asim read rabwa with an open ra, while the other readers use a damma; it means level high ground reached by flowing rivers, where plants grow best.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وعاصم بربوة وإلى ربوة في سورة المؤمنون بفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr lighten the reading of 'it yielded'; others use a doubled consonant, and Nafi and Ibn Kathir also lighten 'its produce.'
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون بالتثقيل

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the garden produced in one year what another garden yields in two.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: حملت في السنة من الريع

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says it bore fruit twice in one year.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: حملت في السنة مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tall means light, gentle rain; al-Suddi identifies it as dew, which falls steadily.
rows.anchor: أي فطش، وهو المطر الضعيف الخفيف ويكون دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden represents a sincere believer's work: God multiplies a pure giver's charity whether small or large, just as the garden yields with either little or heavy rain.
rows.anchor: كذلك يضعف الله صدقة المؤمن المخلص الذي لا يمن ولا يؤذي سواء قلت نفقته أو كثرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even continuous light dew does the work of a strong downpour, and God sees what people do.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الطل إذا كان يدوم يعمل عمل الوابل الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This parable continues the warning against nullifying charity through reminders and harm; the garden owner has a small, weak family.
rows.anchor: أيود يعني: أيحب أحدكم أن تكون له جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An i'sar is a violent whirlwind rising like a column; the burning whirlwind represents a hypocrite's or show-off's apparently good work being destroyed when most needed.
rows.anchor: الريح العاصف التي ترتفع إلى السماء كأنها عمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elderly owner cannot restore the burned garden and his weak children cannot help him, leaving them helpless; likewise, the hypocrite's work is void when no aid, repentance, or reprieve remains.
rows.anchor: فصار أحوج ما يكون إليها وضعف عن إصلاحها لكبره وضعف أولاده

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr narrates that Umar asked the Companions who the garden parable concerned; Ibn Abbas said it represented a show-off, and Umar likened it to a wealthy worshipper whose sins destroy his deeds.
rows.anchor: قال عبيد بن عمير: قال عمر رضي الله عنه يوما لأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Mujahid say the 'good things' to spend are lawful earnings from trade and craft; the verse indicates earnings may be wholesome or corrupt.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه ومجاهد: من حلالات

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that the best food a man eats is from his own earnings, and his child counts among his earnings.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: المقدام بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: Al-Miqdam reports the Prophet saying no food is better than what one earns by hand; David also ate only from his own labor.
rows.anchor: عن المقدام بن معد يكرب أنه حدثه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that unlawful wealth given in charity is not accepted or blessed and becomes provision for the Fire if left behind; evil is not erased by evil.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنهما، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars require annual zakat on trade goods at one quarter of a tenth of their value, once worth twenty dinars or two hundred dirhams; Samura says the Prophet ordered zakat on goods held for sale.
rows.anchor: والزكاة واجبة في مال التجارة عند أكثر أهل العلم، فبعد الحول يقوم العروض

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar treated the hides Himas carried, which he said were his only goods for tanning, as taxable trade property and collected their zakat.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو بن حماس أن أباه قال: مررت بعمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The produce clause requires a tenth on dates, grapes, and staple grains irrigated by rain or a naturally flowing river; costly irrigation reduces it to a half-tenth.
rows.anchor: قيل هذا بإخراج العشور من الثمار والحبوب

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophetic rule: naturally watered or rain-fed crops owe a tenth, while crops watered by irrigation equipment owe half that.
rows.anchor: عن سالم بن عبد الله عن أبيه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عتاب بن أسيد
rows.claim: Attab ibn Asid reports the Prophet's instruction to assess grapes as date palms are assessed, then pay the grape zakat as raisins, just as palm zakat is paid in dates.
rows.anchor: عن عتاب بن أسيد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال في زكاة الكرم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى والشافعي
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Layla and al-Shafii say no tithe is due on crops outside dates, grapes, and staple grains.
rows.anchor: فذهب قوم إلى أنه لا عشر في شيء منها، وهو قول ابن أبي ليلى والشافعي

rows.speaker: الزهري والأوزاعي ومالك
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri, al-Awzai, and Malik require zakat on olives.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري والأوزاعي ومالك رضي الله عنهم: يجب في الزيتون

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa requires a tithe on all vegetables and fruits except grass and firewood.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه: يجب العشر في جميع البقول والخضروات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For fruit, liability begins when it ripens and payment follows harvest and drying; for grain, it begins when firm and is paid after threshing and cleaning.
rows.anchor: وكل ثمرة أوجبنا فيها الزكاة فإنما يجب ببدو الصلاح، ووقت الإخراج بعد الاجتناء والجفاف

rows.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Most scholars require the five-wasq threshold, while Abu Hanifa requires zakat on any amount; the author cites a hadith setting thresholds for dates, silver, and camels.
rows.anchor: ولا يجب العشر في شيء منها حتى تبلغ خمسة أوسق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from Abu Said says no zakat is due on grain or dates until they reach five wasqs; some say this verse concerns voluntary charity instead.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الآية في صدقات التطوع

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that when a believer plants a tree or crop and a person, bird, or animal eats from it, the believer receives charity's reward.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنهم قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir's al-Bazzi doubles the t in tayammamu in connected recitation at 31 Qur'anic locations; other readers use the lighter form, meaning do not deliberately choose.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير برواية البزي بتشديد التاء في الوصل فيها وفي أخواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Ansar hung date bunches in the Prophet's mosque for poor emigrants, and a man added a bunch of inferior dates thinking the abundance made it acceptable; others regularly set aside their worst fruit for charity.
rows.anchor: فنزل فيمن فعل ذلك {ولا تيمموا الخبيث} أي الحشف والرديء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ighmad means making an allowance: one would accept inferior property only by overlooking one's full due; al-Hasan and Qatada say one would not pay the good price for it in a market.
rows.anchor: وأراد هاهنا التجوز والمساهلة، معناه لو كان لأحدكم على رجل حق

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara says a person would accept such inferior produce as a gift only with embarrassment and annoyance, so donors should not give others what they would not accept themselves.
rows.anchor: وروي عن البراء قال: لو أهدي ذلك لكم ما أخذتموه إلا على استحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one's wealth is all good, one may not give the inferior portion because eligible recipients share in one's holdings; if all of it is inferior, it may be given.
rows.anchor: هذا إذا كان المال كله جيدا فليس له إعطاء الرديء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of people's charity and praiseworthy in His actions.
rows.anchor: {واعلموا أن الله غني} عن صدقاتكم {حميد} محمود في أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil promises poverty by frightening people that charity will leave them poor; poverty means bad circumstances and little property, and its root evokes a broken vertebra.
rows.anchor: أن الشيطان يخوفكم بالفقر ويقول للرجل أمسك عليك مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording distinguishes promising good from threatening evil when the object is unspoken; the author illustrates it with verses about promised spoils and the Fire.
rows.anchor: فإذا لم يذكر الخير والشر قلت في الخير: وعدته وفي الشر، أوعدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here indecency means miserliness and withholding zakat; al-Kalbi says indecency elsewhere in the Qur'an means adultery, except in this verse.
rows.anchor: أي بالبخل ومنع الزكاة، وقال الكلبي: كل الفحشاء في القرآن فهو الزنا إلا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness of sins and replacement provision; He is abundant in wealth and knowledge.
rows.anchor: {والله واسع} غني {عليم}

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports God's promise, 'Spend, son of Adam, and I will spend on you'; the Prophet says God's giving never diminishes despite continuous spending since creation.
rows.anchor: أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أسماء
rows.claim: The Prophet told Asma to give without counting or hoarding, lest God withhold from her.
rows.anchor: عن أسماء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are described as believers in God and the Last Day who promote right, forbid wrong, and hasten to good deeds.
rows.anchor: يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر ويأمرون بالمعروف وينهون عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read the verbs 'do' and 'be denied' in the third person; other readers use the second person, and Abu Amr accepts both readings.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص بالياء فيهما إخبار عن الأمة القائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever good they do will not lose its reward: God will acknowledge and repay it; the God-fearing here means believers.
rows.anchor: فلن تعدموا ثوابه بل يشكر لكم وتجازون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers' wealth cannot ransom them and their children cannot aid them against punishment; these are the two means people commonly use to defend themselves.
rows.anchor: لا تدفع أموالهم بالفدية ولا أولادهم بالنصرة شيئا من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are called people of the Fire because they belong to it and never leave, as a companion stays with its associate.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أهلها لا يخرجون منها ولا يفارقونها، كصاحب الرجل لا يفارقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expenditure may mean Abu Sufyan's party spending at Badr and Uhud to oppose the Prophet, or, according to Muqatil, Jews' spending on their scholars.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد نفقات أبي سفيان وأصحابه ببدر وأحد

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says it means all the disbelievers' worldly expenditures and charitable gifts; another view means show-off giving that does not seek God's face.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يعني جميع نفقات الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to gloss ṣirr as a deadly hot wind; another view says it is a sound, while most exegetes say it is intense cold.
rows.anchor: حكي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أنها السموم الحارة التي تقتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop belongs to people who wronged themselves through disbelief, disobedience, and withholding God's due; ṣirr means a severe cold wind in the preferred majority explanation.
rows.anchor: بالكفر والمعصية ومنع حق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers' spending disappears when they need it, like a cold wind or fire destroying a crop before its owners benefit; God does not wrong them, they wrong themselves.
rows.anchor: مثل نفقات الكفار في ذهابها وقت الحاجة إليها كمثل زرع أصابته ريح باردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miserly people should not think their withholding is good; what they withhold will become a creature encircling and biting them on Judgment Day, as Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Wail, al-Shabi, and al-Suddi say.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبي وائل والشعبي والسدي

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's image of unpaid zakat becoming a bald snake with two marks that coils around its owner, bites his cheeks, and says, 'I am your wealth, your treasure.'
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports that unpaid rights on camels, cattle, or sheep make the animals trample and gore their owner on Judgment Day, repeatedly returning until judgment is complete.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه قال: انتهيت إليه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai says the withheld property will become a collar of fire around their necks.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم النخعي: معنى الآية يجعل يوم القيامة في أعناقهم طوقا من النار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they will be ordered on Judgment Day to bring the property they withheld in this world.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يكلفون يوم القيامة أن يأتوا بما بخلوا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Jewish scholars who concealed Muhammad's description and prophethood; their miserliness is concealing knowledge.
rows.anchor: وروى عطية عن ابن عباس: أن هذه الآية نزلت في أحبار اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made to wear what they withheld means bearing its burden and sin, like those who carry their loads on their backs.
rows.anchor: يحملون وزره وإثمه كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits the heavens and earth because He remains after creatures die and their possessions vanish, as another verse says He inherits the earth and everyone on it.
rows.anchor: أنه الباقي الدائم بعد فناء خلقه وزوال أملاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basra and Mecca readers use the third-person 'they do'; the remaining readers address the audience directly.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل البصرة ومكة يعلمون بالياء وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns the heavens and earth and directs them as He wills; He is powerful over everything.
rows.anchor: يصرفها كيف يشاء، {والله على كل شيء قدير}

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet recited these verses repeatedly during the night, praying six long rakats in three pairs and then three witr rakats.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه رقد عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
rows.claim: After night prayer the Prophet asked God for light in his sight, hearing, speech, and around and above and below him; Kuraib's report adds light in the heart and on both sides.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعل في بصري نورا وفي سمعي نورا وفي لساني نورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of understanding are those with intellect; the source segment ends just as their description is introduced.
rows.anchor: ذوي العقول ثم وصفهم فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is not accepted when a sinner reaches the death throes and says, 'I repent now'; neither is it accepted from those who die as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: لا يقبل من كافر إيمان ولا من عاص توبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the people whose faith did not help once they saw God's punishment, and Pharaoh's failed belief as drowning overtook him.
rows.anchor: فلم يك ينفعهم إيمانهم لما رأوا بأسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A'tadna means prepared or made ready.
rows.anchor: أي: هيأنا وأعددنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an warns those who fear, or know, that they will be gathered to God and have no protector or intercessor besides Him; prophets and saints intercede only by God's permission.
rows.anchor: خوف به أي: بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about fearing resurrection may instead mean knowing it, since their fear follows from knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يخافون أي يعلمون، لأن خوفهم إنما كان من علمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no protector or intercessor apart from God; other intercessors act only with His permission.
rows.anchor: ليس لهم من دونه ولي ولا شفيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salman and Khabbab say the verse came after al-Aqra, Uyayna, and their elite group asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers such as Bilal, Suhayb, Ammar, and Khabbab, whose coarse wool clothes they despised.
rows.anchor: قال سلمان وخباب بن الأرت: فينا نزلت هذه الآية، جاء الأقرع بن حابس التميمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the elites demanded a separate meeting and a written promise to remove the poor men, the Prophet refused to drive believers away; Gabriel brought this verse and the command to keep company with those seeking God.
rows.anchor: ما أنا بطارد المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet dropped the sheet, summoned the poor believers, and honored them with God's message of mercy; he thereafter sat close to them and waited for them before leaving.
rows.anchor: فألقى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الصحيفة من يده، ثم دعانا فأثبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet told them he was grateful not to die before being commanded to remain patient with members of his community, saying their life and death were with them.
rows.anchor: الحمد لله الذي لم يمتني حتى أمرني أن أصبر نفسي مع قوم من أمتي

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the petitioners proposed separate days or a single gathering where the Prophet would face them and turn his back on the poor; God revealed the prohibition against dismissing the poor worshippers.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: قالوا له اجعل لنا يوما ولهم يوما، فقال: لا أفعل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh claimed they would follow Muhammad if not for Bilal and Ibn Umm Abd; the verse followed.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: قالت قريش: لولا بلال وابن أم عبد لبايعنا محمدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says morning and evening worship means the dawn and afternoon prayers; he also reports that it can mean all five prayers after elite men asked the poor to pray behind them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني يعبدون ربهم بالغداة والعشي، يعني: صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Said ibn al-Musayyib rejects reading the phrase as a session for public storytellers; he says it refers to the prayer they had just completed.
rows.anchor: مع سعيد بن المسيب، فلما سلم الإمام ابتدر الناس القاص

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhai interprets the phrase as remembering God; another view takes it as literal supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: يعني يذكرون ربهم، وقيل المراد منه: حقيقة الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking God through obedience; Ibn Abbas says they seek God's reward.
rows.anchor: يريدون الله بطاعتهم، قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: يطلبون ثواب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not responsible for the worshippers' account and they are not responsible for his; their livelihood is not his burden, nor is his provision theirs.
rows.anchor: أي: لا تكلف أمرهم ولا يتكلفون أمرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'so you would drive them away' answers the preceding negation; 'then you would be among wrongdoers' answers the prohibition, respectively.
rows.anchor: قوله {فتطردهم} جواب لقوله {ما عليك من حسابهم من شيء}
